nodes.rationale: Real bug case: 'Don't Be Shy' (an Amazon Prime rom-com per its own caption) resolved against TMDB entries that exact-title-match but are unrelated, including an adult-themed 2025 entry, because the existing tiered exact-match scoring only breaks ties by TMDB popularity/rank. Adds a surrounding-caption-text vs. candidate-overview context-based disambiguation step.

nodes.label: Problem B — "Don't Be Shy": strengthened unknown-detection + majority vote
nodes.norm_label: problem b — "don't be shy": strengthened unknown-detection + majority vote
nodes.rationale: The original disambiguate_with_context() prompt never instructed the model it could say 'unknown', and across 8 real live trials it never once did so even when no TMDB candidate plausibly matched the caption -- once landing on an adult-themed entry sharing the exact 'Don't Be Shy' title, since TMDB genuinely lacks the real Alia Bhatt/Amazon Prime film. Fix: (1) prompt now explicitly instructs the model to reply 'unknown' when no candidate's overview plausibly matches; (2) a majority-vote layer samples the identical prompt 3 independent times (_DISAMBIGUATION_SAMPLE_COUNT=3), requiring 2-of-3 agreement before trusting an id -- no majority falls through to the existing pick_best() rank-tiebreak, same as a single honest 'unknown'. Documented 3x chat-client-call cost is scoped narrowly to this one tie-break function, which only fires when 2+ exact-title TMDB matches exist. Explicit honest limitation restated: this cannot make TMDB's data complete -- the real film still isn't in TMDB -- the achievable goal is only to never confidently resolve to a wrong/inappropriate entry.

nodes.label: Final finding — unbounded wait on video_future could leak 2-3 daemon threads per hung download
nodes.norm_label: final finding — unbounded wait on video_future could leak 2-3 daemon threads per hung download
nodes.rationale: _prepare_audio() called video_future.result() unboundedly (no timeout, no cancel_event check). InstagramIngestor.ensure_video() has no cancellation/timeout support at all, and since it now runs unconditionally on every pipeline run, a single reel where yt-dlp's network call genuinely hangs forever leaves _prepare_video's daemon thread blocked forever -- and the unbounded wait in _prepare_audio leaked a second permanently-blocked daemon thread on top, with _cleanup_audio_temp_dir leaking a third. In a long-lived caller (the GUI) this accumulates 2-3 leaked threads per problem reel for the life of the process. Fixed with a 300.0s _VIDEO_DOWNLOAD_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS bound on video_future.result(timeout=...), logging WARNING (not ERROR) and returning None on timeout -- does not fix _prepare_video's own leak if ensure_video() truly never returns (needs yt-dlp cancellation support, out of scope), only stops the leak cascading to 2-3 threads instead of 1.

nodes.label: Fix 1 (HIGH) — unconditional whisper.cpp wiring caused ERROR-log spam on every default run
nodes.norm_label: fix 1 (high) — unconditional whisper.cpp wiring caused error-log spam on every default run
nodes.rationale: build_default_pipeline_deps() constructed a _LazyWhisperCppTranscriber() unconditionally regardless of whether WHISPER_CPP_MODEL_PATH was set. Since most environments (including the dev machine) don't configure whisper.cpp, every run_pipeline/run_pipeline_streaming call triggered a wasted background ffmpeg audio extraction AND a RuntimeError from config.get_whisper_cpp_model_path(), logged via logger.exception at ERROR with a full traceback on every single run. Fixed by only constructing the transcriber when os.environ.get('WHISPER_CPP_MODEL_PATH') is truthy, leaving audio_transcriber as None otherwise -- the same 'capability not available' signal disambiguation_chat_client already uses.

nodes.label: Fix 2 (MEDIUM-HIGH) — uncancellable Anthropic HTTP calls can still hang CLI process exit
nodes.norm_label: fix 2 (medium-high) — uncancellable anthropic http calls can still hang cli process exit
nodes.rationale: AnthropicVisionChatClient.chat() (non-default VISION_BACKEND=anthropic_api) can't honor cancel_event (blocking HTTP call, no local process to kill). Even after Wave 2 moved prep/cleanup jobs to daemon threads, the four actual race jobs and the visual job's nested per-frame frame_executor still ran on real ThreadPoolExecutors, so an in-flight Anthropic call could still hang process exit via either pool. Decision: converted the outer 4-job race pool to daemon threads too (mechanical substitution, exactly 4 jobs/4 workers, no real queueing to preserve) but left the nested frame_executor as a real ThreadPoolExecutor -- it enforces genuine bounded concurrency plus tested cancel_futures/abandon-grace semantics that would be risky to reproduce with raw daemon threads for a benefit that only matters under the non-default backend. Documented as a known, accepted limitation with a test that fails loudly if the gap is ever silently removed.

nodes.label: Follow-up finding A — prompt-corruption bug via chained .replace()
nodes.norm_label: follow-up finding a — prompt-corruption bug via chained .replace()
nodes.rationale: select_primary_candidates() built its prompt via chained .replace() calls on the growing string. Each .replace() rescans the WHOLE string including already-substituted content, so an untrusted source_text (caption/comment/transcript) containing a literal '{candidates}' or '{max_index}' substring got corrupted by a later .replace() matching inside just-inserted text. Fixed by switching to str.format() (one-pass substitution against the original template, matching resolver.py's own already-safe pattern), requiring escaping the prompt's literal JSON-shape example braces.

nodes.label: Bug: `with ThreadPoolExecutor(...)` always calls shutdown(wait=True) on exit
nodes.norm_label: bug: `with threadpoolexecutor(...)` always calls shutdown(wait=true) on exit
nodes.rationale: The first version of Fix 3 wrapped frame detection in `with ThreadPoolExecutor(...) as frame_executor:`, but Executor.__exit__ always calls shutdown(wait=True) regardless of why the block was exited -- so a break on cancellation gave none of the claimed 'stop promptly' benefit; the function still blocked until every submitted detect() call finished. Fixed by managing the executor manually and calling shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True) on the cancelled/exception path. A second follow-up finding caught that cancel_futures=True only drops NOT-YET-STARTED futures -- an already-running detect() call keeps running and the enclosing finally's shutil.rmtree(frames_dir) could delete a file out from under it. Fixed with a bounded wait(frame_futures, timeout=3.0s) before that rmtree runs.

nodes.label: Process-exit correctness: daemon threads vs ThreadPoolExecutor atexit hook
nodes.norm_label: process-exit correctness: daemon threads vs threadpoolexecutor atexit hook
nodes.rationale: concurrent.futures.thread registers a process-wide atexit hook that joins EVERY worker thread of EVERY ThreadPoolExecutor ever created, regardless of that executor's own shutdown(wait=False). Submitting _prepare_video/_prepare_audio to the same pool as the race jobs meant the short-lived reel2movie/cli.py process would hang at exit for however long the download took, even though run_pipeline() itself returned promptly. Fixed by moving those prep/cleanup jobs onto plain daemon=True threads via a new _run_in_daemon_thread() helper, since daemon threads aren't tracked by that atexit hook; the four actual race jobs stay on the ThreadPoolExecutor since the orchestrator genuinely needs to track/cancel them.

nodes.label: Fix 1 — video download + audio extraction no longer block the race
nodes.norm_label: fix 1 — video download + audio extraction no longer block the race
nodes.rationale: Before: _prepare_video_and_audio() ran synchronously BEFORE _race_candidate_jobs() submitted anything, so every reel paid for a full yt-dlp download + ffmpeg extraction even when caption/comment extraction would have won almost instantly -- directly undercutting the rewrite's point (user's stated complaint: 'it's taking too long'). After: video download and audio extraction become two more concurrently-started jobs; only the audio-transcript and visual jobs block on them, internally, via a polling _wait_or_cancelled() helper (a plain unbounded .result() wait was tried first and proven by a failing test to reintroduce the exact blocking the fix exists to remove). Non-winning race jobs get a bounded 2.0s grace period to react to cancel_event.

nodes.label: Bug: real pipe-buffer deadlock in run_cancelable()
nodes.norm_label: bug: real pipe-buffer deadlock in run_cancelable()
nodes.rationale: The poll loop called bare proc.wait(timeout=...), which unlike communicate() never drains stdout/stderr. A child writing more than ~64KB combined output before exiting blocks on write() with nothing draining the other end, so wait() just kept timing out until the full timeout_seconds budget elapsed and the process was killed -- the exact deadlock subprocess's own docs warn about. Reproduced directly (200KB stdout child, timeout=5) hanging the full 5s instead of finishing in milliseconds; not caught by the existing test suite since no prior test exercised non-trivial child output. Fixed by switching the poll loop to repeated proc.communicate(timeout=poll_interval_seconds) calls, which is explicitly safe per communicate()'s own docs and loses no output; repro then completed in ~70ms. Added a permanent regression test.

nodes.label: Frame sampling interval 1.0s -> 0.5s
nodes.rationale: _DEFAULT_FRAME_INTERVAL_SECONDS changed 1.0 -> 0.5 based on empirical A/B testing against 3 real sample Instagram Reels: halving the interval caught meaningfully more brief on-screen-text/poster cards (held only 1-2s, falling between sparse samples) at a 22%-58% increase in vision-LLM call count. Going denser still (0.2s) was tested and rejected as +26%-248% more calls for diminishing catch rate.
